cards.front: Poder and Querer — what kind of verbs are they?
cards.back:
Both are modal verbs (like English 'can' and 'want') that are followed by an infinitive:
PODER — can / to be able to: Puedo bailar. (I can dance.)
QUERER — to want / to love: Quiero bailar. (I want to dance.)
cards.grammarNote: Both are stem-changing verbs: poder is o→ue, querer is e→ie. Only the infinitive form is regular.

cards.back:
yo puedo
tú puedes
él/ella/usted puede
nosotros podemos
vosotros podéis
ellos/ellas/ustedes pueden
cards.grammarNote: Stem changes o→ue in all forms except nosotros and vosotros (the 'shoe verb' pattern).

cards.back:
yo quiero
tú quieres
él/ella/usted quiere
nosotros queremos
vosotros queréis
ellos/ellas/ustedes quieren
cards.grammarNote: Stem changes e→ie in all forms except nosotros and vosotros. Querer also means 'to love' with people.

cards.front: Can I buy you a drink?
cards.back:
¿Te puedo invitar a una copa?
or
¿Puedo invitarte a una copa?
cards.grammarNote: The object pronoun te can go before the conjugated verb or attached to the infinitive — both are correct. Invitar a una copa = to treat to a drink.

cards.front: Can I have your phone number?
cards.back: ¿Me puedes dar tu número de teléfono?
cards.grammarNote: Me puedes dar — 'can you give me?' The indirect object pronoun me goes before puedes. This is polite and natural.

cards.front: Would you like to dance with me?
cards.grammarNote: Quieres (tú form) + bailar (infinitive) + conmigo (with me). ¿Quieres...? is the most natural way to ask someone to dance.

cards.front: I want to dance with you.
cards.grammarNote: Quiero + infinitive — very direct and sincere. Contigo (with you, informal) is a contracted prepositional pronoun.

cards.front: We can go to the festival together.
cards.grammarNote: Podemos (nosotros form) + ir (infinitive). Al = a + el (contraction). Juntos (together, m.pl.).

cards.front: She wants to stay until midnight.
cards.back: Ella quiere quedarse hasta la medianoche.
cards.grammarNote: Quiere + quedarse (reflexive infinitive). The reflexive pronoun se stays attached to the infinitive here.

cards.front: I can't leave yet — the night is just getting started.
cards.back: No puedo irme todavía — la noche apenas está empezando.
cards.grammarNote: No + puedo makes it negative — no puedo irme (I can't leave). Todavía means 'yet/still.' Apenas = 'just/barely.'

cards.front: Do you want to go out with me sometime?
cards.grammarNote: Quieres + salir (infinitive). Algún día = someday/sometime. Conmigo = with me (contracted form).

cards.front: I can and I want to be here all night.
cards.back: Puedo y quiero estar aquí toda la noche.
cards.grammarNote: Two modals can share one infinitive — puedo y quiero estar (I can and want to be). Toda la noche = all night.
Querer + a + person = to love someone romantically. The personal a is required before novia. Te quiero (I love you) is the intimate declaration.

cards.front: Could I ask you something? / Would you like to...?
cards.back:
¿Podría preguntarte algo? / ¿Querrías...?
or (more common)
¿Puedo preguntarte algo? / ¿Quieres...?
cards.grammarNote: The conditional (podría/querrías) is more formal/polite. In casual nightlife situations, the present tense (puedo/quieres) sounds more natural and confident.

cards.front: Translate: I want to dance, but I can't — I have to find my brothers.
cards.back: Quiero bailar, pero no puedo — tengo que encontrar a mis hermanos.
cards.grammarNote: Quiero + bailar (want to dance). No puedo (can't). Tener que + infinitive = have to. Personal a before mis hermanos (specific people).
